Subject: Vendor privacy annex and DPIA checklist for AI hosting (Redwood Inference)

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement and our legal/privacy team asked me to gather a short set of items we need to proceed with an RFP for AI hosting across our campus services. Overall we are treating this as a FedRAMP-adjacent procurement (we are not a federal agency, but our state grants require similar controls). Can you confirm the following as succinctly as possible?

1) Do you have a current SOC 2 Type II report and a CAIQ/consensus assessment snapshot we can review?
2) We will run a DPIA for the pilot. Please share any DPIA checklist items you recommend (data flow diagrams, retention, deletion SLA for student PII, subprocessor list).
3) Are you able to sign our privacy annex that includes SCCs (standard contractual clauses) and a clause for data residency (we need EU data at-rest only in eu-west-1 for some research projects)?
4) HIPAA: we may route some health-adjacent student services through the system. Do you have a HIPAA BA agreement template or notes on applicability?

If you can send the SOC2 + CAIQ and a draft DPA/privacy annex redline we will fast-track legal reviews. We are hoping to get answers by Wednesday so we can scope the DPIA.

Appreciate the quick help — happy to hop on a 20-minute call if easier.

Ellie Morris
Contracts & Procurement
Midwest State University

Ellie —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, and I attached the artifacts you requested. Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025.pdf, CAIQ_Snapshot_Jan2026.xlsx, Redwood_DPA_Annex_v1.2.docx (DPA annex = our proposed annex that includes SCCs and processors list).

1) SOC 2: Yes — Type II, most recent reporting period ended Dec 31, 2025. Redacted auditor contact info removed for the public copy; we can provide an NDA-delivered copy with full auditor appendix if required.

2) DPIA checklist & guidance: we generally recommend the DPIA include (we've put a short checklist in the DPA annex and attached CAIQ for control references):
   - Data flow diagram (ingress points, transient KV cache, persistent storage)
   - Data minimization and retention matrix (we support configurable retention per customer; default token logs 30 days, audit logs retained 90 days unless otherwise negotiated)
   - Deletion SLA: API-based bulk delete with 30-day completion window for indexed content; immediate deletion for config records. We can negotiate shorter windows for regulated workloads.
   - Subprocessor list: included in the DPA annex (S3-equivalent object storage provider, telemetry analytics provider, CDN).

3) SCCs and residency: The annex includes standard SCCs and an option to add a binding clause requiring eu-west-1 at-rest storage for specified projects. Note: compute may still route through other regions for inference unless customer selects a private VPC/dedicated deployment — we call that out in section 4.2.

4) HIPAA: We support HIPAA workloads via Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem). We have a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) template; I've CC'd our Privacy lead Mina to follow up with the BAA and any additional control proofs you need.

Next steps I propose:
- Review the attached DPA annex and redline in the document. If you want an initial redline from our counsel I can ask them to prepare one.
- If the DPIA team wants a short technical session to walk through data flows (15–30 min), we can set that up this week.

If you want me to send the auditor copy of SOC2 via a secure link, say the word and we will spin that up.

Best,

Ellie —

Appreciate the follow-up. Quick answers from legal/compliance team below; Mina will attach the BAA and a short subprocessor flow-down statement after internal review.

- KV cache behavior: By default, the serving runtime holds an in-memory KV cache per request session for latency (ephemeral) and does not persist user identifiers to long-term storage. Multi-turn context is stored transiently in cache; any persisted context requires explicit API parameters (we call them session_persist flags) or use of our Dedicated/private deployment where customers control persistence. We will confirm the exact retention TTLs in the annex language if you need stricter defaults.

- SCCs: Our annex references the EU Commission Standard Contractual Clauses (2021). We will include the 2021 text in the DPA annex and can mirror your preferred clause variant in the redline.

- On-site audits: For pilot customers we typically offer remote evidence reviews plus a quarterly audit window. For state institutions with on-site audit needs we can discuss a scoped on-site review with mutual NDAs and advance notice; cost-recovery for on-site travel applies. If you can provide a short audit scope and timebox (e.g., 1-day on-site, controls list), we will confirm feasibility.

Mina (copied) — please send the BAA template and subprocessor flow-down confirmation to Ellie.

If Ellie is OK with our proposed audit alternative, we can get an initial redline to you by EOD Thursday and schedule a 20-minute DPIA walkthrough for Friday.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
